newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE PESO ENDS DOWN IN EDGY MARKET.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE PESO ENDS DOWN IN EDGY MARKET.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended weak on Tuesday as the fall in the region's currencies prodded banks to buy the dollar again, traders said.
"They're buying the dollar in anticipation the peso might depreciate," a dealer said.
The peso was also under pressure from the seasonal high demand by importers, traders said.
The peso finished at 28.66, near the day's low of 28.67. It's previous day's close was at 28.57. Volume doubled to $102 million from $56.2 million.
Traders said the peso did not get much support from the central bank which only sold about $4.0 million at 28.59/28.60.
It was also not helped by the news that Thailand was able to get pledges of $16 billion in loans to aid its ailing economy since the market had long expected this.
Traders said the peso could trade in a lower range of 28.60/28.70 on Wednesday.
